confirmed.evidence:
Reproduced with a throwaway vitest test, since deleted: tests/web/tmp_repro/focusReload.test.tsx, run with `npx vitest run tests/web/tmp_repro --reporter=verbose`. HEAD is 63fbc2d. Its only differences from a6b0b23 are in docs and e2e files; Focus.tsx is the same. The test renders Focus on a 40-slide deck with stub APIs, waits for the first 40 thumbFor calls to finish, then sends deck.changed followed by lane.updated. laneService.accept emits them in that order (src/server/laneService.ts:60 and emitLane at :130). Output:

gap=0ms  initial=40 afterAccept: getDeck=2 thumbFor=40 distinct=40
gap=30ms initial=40 afterAccept: getDeck=2 thumbFor=48 distinct=40

Confirmed:
- Every deck.changed and every lane.updated/lane.closed for the lane runs reload() (web/src/screens/Focus.tsx:137-138).
- reload() fetches deck, lane and preview again, then makes one sequential thumbFor call per slide for the whole deck (Focus.tsx:123-127). Nothing is reused. After one accept, all 40 slides are re-requested even though the stub hashes are unchanged.
- Server side: GET /api/thumbs/for/:id (src/server/routes/thumbs.ts:15-18) calls thumbHash → hashFor (src/render/thumbs.ts:203). For every request, hashFor rebuilds the HTML, re-runs sha256 over every font buffer, and reads and hashes every asset file from disk.

Overstated:
- "~80+ requests" is too high. The generation guard (gen !== generation.current, Focus.tsx:116/125) stops the first loop once the second reload starts. If the two events arrive together, you get about 40 requests (one full loop). With a 30ms gap you get about 48 (part of the first loop, then the full second one). Two full loops do not happen.
- Font bytes are loaded once and kept in memory (loadFonts is memoized with ??=, thumbs.ts:125). They are still re-hashed on every request; they are not re-read from disk. Asset files are re-read from disk on every request.

Net: each event costs about O(deck size) thumb requests, each re-hashing fonts and assets. The "2x" multiplier in the claim is wrong.
confirmed.fix_hint: In Focus.reload, only call thumbFor for slides whose content changed or that have no thumb yet (keep a per-slide content stamp as Main's shownSlides does). On the server, cache the per-font and per-asset digests (keyed by mtime) instead of re-hashing them on every request.

Nothing checks `disposed` on this path, so query #2 starts after dispose(). Nothing ever aborts it, which is why the run hung until the 30s timeout.

Test 2: first a good arc run stores "EARLIER ARC REMARK". A second run('arc') is then disposed mid-query, and the retry fails fast.

  REPRO query #2 started; signal.aborted=false

  REPRO run result: ["check arc failed: spawn failed"]
  REPRO after: ["check:arc: check arc failed: spawn failed"]
So the disposed run makes two queryImpl calls, and persist() still runs: the earlier arc remark is replaced by a failure remark. Because the retry itself was never aborted, the stored text carries the retry's own error, not 'interrupted'. It would read 'interrupted' only if something aborted the retry. Pending lanes that the check owns would also be closed at runner.ts:368, since persist() goes through the same path. I read that from the code; I did not run it.
